save.nonExchangeableAssets: Persistent list of store-purchased asset keys that are not eligible for Exchange; retained independently of the rolling transaction history.

delivery.offline: after assets are cached; not yet guaranteed

notes: Generation 1.32 public demo candidate (2026-11-15): N.U Casino now reads spendable assets from the shared wallet, allows a 1..balance base wager, applies the resettable 1x/2x/4x/8x double-up ladder, and records wager/payout as separate outgoing/incoming rows with a casino round ID. Existing game payout rules are preserved. Casino rounds are not core-game Waves. Local virtual demo only; no real-money flows or server ledger.

Generation 1 public demo candidate (2026-11-15): core games settle rewards and gameplay costs as per-Wave, per-asset/category local wallet rows with idempotency keys; interrupted Waves are recovered on reload. Store purchase and capsule use create separate incoming/outgoing rows. Human acceptance evidence is collected through the separate QA process; no internal report-download control is exposed in the player UI. This is browser-local test state only; server wallet, cloud sync, production-grade idempotency and human/device acceptance remain pending.

Generation 1 Exchange wallet bridge: reads the canonical nu-world-save-v1 profile, asset rows, unpriced X/N fields and recent transactions. Game manifests are discovered on launcher startup and reconciled after wallet saves / module inventory events. Protocol metadata only; no shadow wallet or settlement.

Generation 1 Exchange visual refinement: adds a restrained ambient background-flow animation derived from recent local economic behavior, bounded to ±3 index points and 3 display-volume units, plus player-drawn trend/horizontal/vertical lines and shaded analysis zones. All ambient pulses and drawings are presentation-only and never write wallet transactions.

Generation 1.35 candidate (2026-11-15): Gateway is the single in-game navigation gate with Back, Menu and Profile one-click actions. Opening it freezes the game round and all ambient renderers until a decision; duplicate in-game navigation buttons are hidden. The centered menu lists concise module titles with keyboard keycaps: player modules first, then Painting, Random Game and the three core games. Store-purchased assets are durably excluded from Exchange selectors and virtual market charts. Latest Exchange chart controls (zoom, grid, wicks, volume, moving average, themes, palettes and parametric bands) are preserved.

Generation 1 unified profile workshop preview (2026-11-14): preserves the historical four-field card and exposes all current profile design alternatives for human comparison: hue, neutral white/dark tint, selected-color lightness and optional saturation; exact age, age band, both or no age; Bio and Interests; optional/local-identity-required/required public-card models; per-field privacy and share-consent preview; private-view YES/NO and fake passphrase flow; appearance-only, appearance-plus-fields and full lock policies; card/HUD/Wallet/hidden stats placement; holographic materials, typography, geometry, glow, transparency, scanlines, texture, motion, reduced effects, high contrast and device quality; local image fit and 2x4 crop-anchor/photo-slot semantics; recovery choices; platform and launcher delivery alternatives; local save, export protection, import validation and future sync models; reduced-effects and high-contrast accessibility previews. All are temporary preview controls that reset on close. No credentials are authenticated, no data is saved/exported/imported/recovered, no image is uploaded and no network sync/share occurs.

Generation 1.33 candidate: Exchange now includes a fictional activity-driven virtual market simulator with OHLC candles, volume, demand/supply and N.U-only index; it derives every movement from the local player transaction ledger and never uses real-world financial data.
Generation 1.32.1: remove duplicate legacy menu/back buttons from main-world internal views so the shared hex gateway is the single navigation entry point.

Generation 1.32: calibrates the shared N.U hex gateway across all internal Generation 1 pages with responsive positioning, touch-direct activation, mouse-hover dwell, two-step click/keyboard confirmation, outside-exit tolerance and pause/blur behavior. Navigation only; game rules and wallet/save state are unchanged.

Generation 1.31: adds a standalone N.U Casino with playable Coin Flip, Lucky Dice and Mini Slots. The casino uses a separate local virtual-credit balance (100 starting credits), persists in the shared browser save, and never touches XP/Mana or real money. Human browser/device acceptance remains required.

Generation 1.16: the Mana Collector uses five preserved N.U Material SVG assets as crisp pixel-art glints around interactive Mana targets and emits a short material-based collection burst. Other game mechanics and the adaptive runtime remain unchanged; human visual/touch QA is required.

Generation 1.15: image analysis now describes the visible four-layer composite; PNG and SVG exports include a companion Markdown human report, SVG embeds the report metadata, and Graphic IR includes the report as humanReport. A direct human-report download is also available. Source image processing remains local.

Generation 1.14 candidate: Studio workspace uses deterministic fit geometry and ResizeObserver sizing; pointer mapping is centralized; import shows an original-source preview, preserves a separate working copy, offers smooth/nearest resampling and optional Floyd–Steinberg dithering; import size is bounded at 25 MB. Game HUD asset-profile interactions no longer bubble into gameplay pointer handlers and the profile is positioned beside the active resource bar. Browser acceptance remains pending.

Game HUD now exposes per-game asset profiles on hover/focus; each profile is a filtered projection of the global wallet, not a separate balance store. HP capsule can be purchased or used from the Store and used from the in-game HP icon.

Generation 1.13 candidate: Studio fixes fit-to-view/zoom/scroll and per-pixel checkerboard; adds pencil, eraser, fill, eyedropper, line, rectangle, ellipse and brush sizing; imports up to 256px longest-edge with up to 32 colors; exports SVG, PNG and NU-GFX-IR/1; unique artwork downloads award a bounded 1–25 shared XP reward once per fingerprint to the same local Generation 1 wallet.

Generation 1.12 candidate: Pixel Art Studio adds local high-detail aspect-preserving image import, weighted median-cut palette reduction, alpha cutoff, contour-based closed SVG paths with transparent-hole preservation, and pixel-run export. Source images remain local; no upload or server processing.

Generation 1.11 candidate: adds a local, testable wallet transaction boundary, HP capsule purchase/consumption feedback, owned-asset wallet view and local player identity card; no server account or real-money economy.

Generation 1.10: Pixel Art Studio now uses N.U graphics capability budgets, independent resizable workspace frame, zoom control, rectangular pixel-art dimensions, aspect-ratio lock, nearest-neighbor artwork resizing, and adaptive editable-pixel limits. Original source files remain untouched; only local working copies are resampled.
Generation 1.9 candidate: added N.U Pixel Art Studio as a separate creative tool in the main library; it is deliberately excluded from the three-game random gameplay pool.
Generation 1.8 development: repaired literal newline escaping in the store/game script so the JavaScript parses as source text.
N.U public-test candidate retains the adaptive/network runtime unchanged and keeps the public default branch untouched until the candidate is merged.
Generation 1.7 development: added N.U Store navigation and a first-visit two-choice store guide shell; no unavailable/locked upgrades are displayed.
Generation 1.7 development: removed duplicate persistent round counters; 1/10–10/10 feedback is object-local after successful interaction.
Generation 1.7 development: removed floating XP/Mana/reward labels from object interactions; +1 capsule-edge feedback remains.
Generation 1.7 development: online reading layout retains central spawn exclusion; downloadable full-screen builds may set data-delivery=download to remove it.
This is an experimental browser prototype, not a production game release.
N-BI consumes 10 Mana per successful Chaos shot in the current prototype; upgrade-based cost reduction is not yet implemented.
No server account or cloud save exists.
Random game is selected on each fresh launch; a running round stays fixed until ended or page reload.
Generation 1.4 adds an independent 320x180 pixel-art city layer with local dawn/day/dusk/night phases and reduced-motion handling.
The adaptive runtime file remains unchanged; pixel-world quality is adjusted after the existing calibration.
Pixel skyline is procedural placeholder art and is not yet a canonical, source-confirmed Niroo City illustration.
Generation 1.5 expands the renderer into a layered, source-neutral landscape with a moving sun arc, night-only stars, river, forest, coast, fields, city terraces and distant traffic.
Mouse camera follows pointer after first mouse movement; touch camera activates after first touch gesture and uses inverse drag. Drag gestures are excluded from game interactions.
Chaos targets now advance toward the defensive boundary; each unneutralized mass causes one HP damage and is removed. A successful N-BI interaction neutralizes one mass.
Generation 1.5 adds separate mouse-follow and inverse touch-drag camera input; drag gestures are excluded from gameplay interactions.
Unneutralized Chaos masses move toward the defensive boundary; each mass crossing causes one HP damage and then disappears.
Niroo City terrain geography in the renderer is a non-canonical visual proposal based on published urban descriptions; see NU-WORLD-VISUAL-BIBLE-G1.5.md.
Generation 1.6: successful object interactions show an exact n/10 marker at the clicked object's location.
Chaos approach speed doubles by target sequence (1, 2, 4, 8; capped at 8); every mass not neutralized that reaches the boundary causes 1 HP damage.
Completing a full 10-interaction game round restores 1 HP up to the maximum of 10.
XP rail spans the bottom edge; Mana capsule rail is placed at the left side above it; HP display now includes a moving ECG-style scanner trace.
Aircraft are placed in an upper altitude band and road traffic in a ground band to reduce intersections with buildings.
The nine Mana capsule upgrade levels and N-BI shot-cost reduction are not yet implemented; current Chaos shot still costs 10 Mana.

The city layout is an art-direction proposal, not a canonical map. Published sources describe Niroo City as green, engineered, sustainable, and founded by Binam Binshun, but do not establish a definitive skyline layout.

Generation 1.34 candidate: Exchange replay selectors use number-free seconds/minutes/hours/days/weeks/months labels; player controls chart zoom across the retained 24 local steps, grid, candle shadows, volume, moving-average overlays, day/night mode and packaged palettes. Candle wick tolerance is deterministic and display-only (up to ±5 N.U index points).

Exchange refinement: optional neutral-grey parametric dispersion bands show rolling mean ± one standard deviation from recorded candle closes; a local wallet-ledger change restarts the replay cursor and pulses the chart. Both are presentation-only.

libraryTools.name: N.U Creative Studio — Pixel Art & Vector Lab
libraryTools.purpose: Local raster analysis, non-destructive pixel editing, contour SVG, palette-indexed tiles, run-length spans, edge/region maps and machine-readable N.U graphics instructions; downloadable human-readable image report with palette, transparency, connected-region bounds and export notes

libraryTools.name: N.U Casino — Mini Games
libraryTools.purpose: Three playable browser mini-games: Coin Flip, Lucky Dice and Mini Slots. Uses a separate local virtual-credit balance; no real-money deposits, payments or cash-outs.

generation1Exchange.assets: Only wallet-backed Generation 1 assets are listed; no placeholder coin is invented.
generation1Exchange.crossGameChange: Prepared registry for Launcher game adapters; transfer settlement remains disabled until two compatible approved game adapters exist.

history.cache: Dedicated local exchange cache rebuilt from the local wallet on refresh; underlying wallet ledger is not truncated.

generation1Exchange.cooldown: Ten successful operations may complete in one Exchange visit; the 11th attempted operation starts a 120-second cooldown. Leaving before the 11th attempt resets the in-memory visit count.
generation1Exchange.maintenanceLock: Cross-game transfer module is locked by default. A two-step local maintenance latch is a UX safeguard only, not authentication or anti-cheat.
generation1Exchange.note: Fictional N.U-only activity visualization. Replay speed changes presentation only and never fabricates wallet events or real-world financial data. Ambient flow is a bounded, player-behavior-shaped visual layer (±3 index points and at most 3 display-volume units) and is not recorded as transactions. Player chart annotations are local presentation preferences only.

chartControls.parametricBands: rolling mean ± one standard deviation; display-only
chartControls.ledgerChangeResponse: restart replay cursor and pulse chart on actual local transaction add/remove; no synthetic transactions

generation1Exchange.visualWickTolerance: Deterministic display-only range of up to ±5 N.U index points; it never changes candle close, wallet balances or transactions.
generation1Exchange.storePurchasePolicy: Store-purchased assets are durably marked in save.nonExchangeableAssets and remain non-exchangeable even after the rolling 24-transaction history expires. They are excluded from wallet asset selectors, local balance history charts and the virtual market simulator. The purchased asset remains owned in the Wallet; the purchase currency debit remains an ordinary wallet transaction.

chartTools.annotationStorage: Local chart preference only; keyed per asset; never written to wallet/save ledger.

navigation.future: Other sections may receive their own access-controlled Gateway analogue only after separate approval.

healthProbe.purpose: small reachability response used by runtime and launcher checks; contains no player data
